title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Grothendieck's own manuscript on motives in Tannakian language, probably c.1965–67. The neighbouring 'pages' are typescript from an unrelated English thesis on the Brauer group of a ringed space, filed in the same folder, so the page's own context is missing. The opening 'degrés positifs' continues a sentence from a lost previous page, presumably the definition of an 'effective' i.

Setting (modern reading):
- M is a Tannakian category of motives (or a Hodge-type analogue), with a fibre functor E ↦ E( ) to vector spaces over C.
- G is its Tannakian (motivic Galois) group.
- i: G_m → G_C is a cocharacter λ ↦ i(λ). Through the fibre functor it puts a grading on each E( ).
- ε: G → G_m is the weight (Tate) character, with ⟨i,ε⟩ = ν defined by ε(i(λ)) = λ^ν.
- Λ(-1) is the Tate/Lefschetz motive and E(n) denotes Tate twists.

Call i 'effective' if the i-grading has only degrees ≥ 0 on the relevant generators. Statements on the page:
1. If i is effective, so are its conjugates by g ∈ G(C) and its conjugates by automorphisms of C, in particular the complex-conjugate cocharacter ī. This is the Hodge picture: μ and μ̄ together control p ≥ 0 and q ≥ 0.
2. For fixed i, let P(i) be the strictly full subcategory of M of objects E whose i-grading on E( ) has only non-negative degrees. Then:
   - P(i) is stable under ⊕, subobjects (and quotients) and ⊗, and contains the unit object.
   - It contains Λ(-1) if ε(i) := ⟨i,ε⟩ ≥ 0.
   - If ⟨i,ε⟩ > 0, every E ∈ M has a Tate twist E(n) lying in P(i).
3. Programme, only partly legible in the struck-out and boxed lines: consider the family T_i of G(C)-conjugates i∘int(g) of a cocharacter. The subcategory M^+ of effective motives should be the intersection of the P(i) over such a family. Conversely, a full subcategory M^+ satisfying these axioms (stable under ⊕, ⊗, subobjects; contains 1 and Λ(-1); every object becomes effective after a Tate twist) should be described as such an intersection. Possibly some extra 'graduation' condition is needed.

Purpose: an intrinsic, group-theoretic description of 'effective' motives inside the rigid Tannakian category of all motives, modelled on effective Hodge structures (H^{p,q} ≠ 0 only for p,q ≥ 0, via the Hodge cocharacter and its conjugate). This would let one recover the non-rigid tensor category of effective motives from (G, ε, a conjugation-stable set of cocharacters).

In modern terms the axioms describe a sub-tensor-category whose 'Tannakian dual' is a monoid M̄ ⊃ G. Effective representations are those extending to the closure of the cones generated by the conjugates of i, as in Vinberg/Renner reductive monoids.
errors: 'contient 0' is almost certainly 'contient 1' (the unit object). The zero object is trivially in P(i); the point is the unit.
Conjugating i by automorphisms of C only makes sense if G (and the fibre functor) is defined over a subfield such as Q, so that Aut(C) acts on G(C) and on cocharacters. This is implicit, not stated.
Whether Λ(-1) lies in P(i) when ⟨i,ε⟩ ≥ 0 depends on the sign convention for the weight character (Λ(1) vs Λ(-1)). Not checkable from the page.

The converse claim (every M^+ satisfying the axioms is an intersection of P(i)'s) is not proved and is false in general without further hypotheses, e.g. reductivity and a saturation condition. The page itself hesitates: 'peut être une des conditions de graduation'.

ideas.what: Grading of the fibre functor by a cocharacter i: G_m → G; a sub-tensor-category P(i) of objects with non-negative i-degrees
ideas.modern_name: Gradings/filtrations of Tannakian categories by cocharacters; Hodge cocharacter μ and effectivity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (Catégories tannakiennes, 1972); Deligne (Hodge II/III, Mumford–Tate groups)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck supervised Saavedra's thesis; no Grothendieck text with this

ideas.what: Effective subcategory M^+ of a Tannakian category of motives characterized by axioms (⊕, ⊗, subobjects, contains 1 and Λ(-1), every object effective after a Tate twist) and realized as an intersection of P(i) over a conjugation-stable set of cocharacters
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian description of effective motives / effective Hodge structures; Tannaka duality for monoids (reductive monoid containing the motivic Galois group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Partly folklore; Nori's effective motives (diagram categories, Huber–Müller-Stach); Tannaka duality for monoids (e.g. Saavedra-style reconstruction for non-rigid categories); Vinberg/Renner monoids
ideas.where_published: unsure; not in Saavedra as far as I know

ideas.what: Stability of effectivity under G(C)-conjugation and under Aut(C), in particular complex conjugation ī
ideas.modern_name: Hodge cocharacter and its complex conjugate; effective = p,q ≥ 0

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an axiomatic characterization of the effective subcategory M^+ of a Tannakian category of motives. He proposes realizing it as an intersection of 'positivity' subcategories P(i) attached to a conjugation-stable family of cocharacters, with Tate twisting making every object effective. This amounts to describing effective motives via a monoid (cone of cocharacters) attached to the motivic Galois group with its weight character. The converse classification is left unfinished.
missed.quote: la sous-catégorie pleine P(i) de M formée des E tels que E( ) ait une i-graduation positive est st. pleine, stable par ... ⊗, contient [1], et Λ(-1) si ... ε(i) ≥ 0, et satisfait la condition que ∀E ∈ Ob M, ∃n tel que E(n) ∈ Ob P(i), si on suppose ε(i) > 0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The relation between effective motives (Nori's effective category, Ayoub's motivic Galois monoid questions) and positivity cones of cocharacters in the motivic Galois group is not systematically worked out. A Tannakian 'effective = intersection of cocharacter positivity conditions' theorem would give a clean monoid/Vinberg-type description of effective motives and Hodge structures. It is at least a little-known early instance of this idea, attributed to nobody.

missed.claim: The page implicitly links effectivity of motives with one-parameter-subgroup positivity, of the kind found in Hilbert–Mumford and in reductive monoid theory, through the Hodge cocharacter and its Galois/complex conjugates.
missed.quote: si i est effectif, il en est de même de ses conjugués par éléments de G(C), et de ses conjugués par automorphismes de C, en particulier de ī
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests describing the effective motivic monoid as determined by Galois orbits of 'Hodge-type' cocharacters, a bridge between motivic Galois theory and reductive monoids that seems little explored.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early, probably mid-1960s, Tannakian treatment of effective motives via cocharacter positivity and weight pairings. The ingredients (cocharacter gradings, Hodge cocharacter, Tate twists) became standard through Saavedra and Deligne. However, the specific programme of characterizing M^+ axiomatically as an intersection of P(i) over conjugate cocharacters is not, to my knowledge, in the literature in this form. It is a fragmentary sketch, so the surprise is moderate.
transcription_corrections: 'contient 0' should likely read 'contient 1' (unit object), followed by 'et Λ(-1)'.
Line 7 likely reads 'stable par ⊕, par quotients, sous-objets, par ⊗' rather than 'stable par ⊗ ..., par ⊕'.
The boxed insertion near T_i reads 'i∘int(g)∘i'; probably intended 'i ↦ int(g)∘i' (conjugates of i by g ∈ G(C)).
'Par intersection de ces foncteurs' is perhaps 'Par intersection de ces sous-catégories'.
The neighbouring pages (English typescript on the Brauer group of a ringed space) are unrelated material filed in the same folder, not the continuation of this manuscript.
